In mathematics, the '''Gelfand–Zeitlin system''' (also written '''Gelfand–Zetlin system''', '''Gelfand–Cetlin system''', '''Gelfand–Tsetlin system''') is an [[integrable system]] on conjugacy classes of Hermitian matrices. It was introduced by {{harvs|txt|last1=Guillemin|last2=Sternberg|year=1983}}, who named it after the [[Restricted representation#Gelfand–Tsetlin basis|Gelfand–Zeitlin basis]], an early example of [[canonical basis]], introduced by [[I. M. Gelfand|Israel Gelfand]] and [[Michael Tsetlin]] in 1950s. {{harvs|txt|last1=Kostant|last2=Wallach|year=2006}} introduced a complex version of this integrable system.
